housing: Barnsley is a former coalfield borough in South Yorkshire, running from the Dearne valley in the east to Pennine moorland around Penistone in the west. Much of the housing is brick terraces from the mining era, inter- and post-war council estates and new-build estates near the M1. Prices are well below the England average. Private rented homes are often older terraces in the Dearne towns and around the town centre, while Penistone and the western villages have stone-built houses.
checkinTips: Brick terraces in the Dearne towns: photograph back yards, rear doors, outhouses and the shared ginnels behind the rows.
Former mining areas: photograph any cracks in walls, sticking doors or uneven floors so later movement can be compared.
Stone-built homes around Penistone and the Pennine villages: photograph window reveals, walls and chimney breasts for damp, and any stove or open fire.
Exposed hill properties: photograph gutters, downpipes and roof edges visible from the ground, and note heating controls and how they work.
Ex-council semis: photograph uPVC windows and doors, their locks and the number of keys, and garden fences and sheds.
tenantHelp: Tenants in Barnsley can contact Barnsley Council’s private sector housing team about disrepair, damp or unsafe conditions in a rented home.
